fields.meta_description: Describe your claims process. Emergent builds insurance claims automation that reads repair estimates and holds large settlements for approval.
fields.h1: Build Insurance Claims Automation for Your Claims Team
fields.hero_description: Get insurance claims automation that opens each claim from the first report and assigns the right adjuster.
fields.features_heading: The Parts of a Working Claims App
fields.features_subheading: Six parts that take repeat work off your adjusters. Whether a loss is covered stays a decision people make.
fields.feature_1:
A loss report, one question per screen

Policyholders answer one question per screen: the date and place of the loss, what was damaged, and how it happened. Photos come last, then the claim number shows on screen.
fields.feature_2:
Assignment by loss type and territory

Each claim opens in the queue of the adjuster who handles that loss type and territory. A Slack or email alert tells them a new file is waiting, with the photos attached.
fields.feature_3:
Estimates and invoices read into fields

Repair estimates and invoices are read into line items and totals as they are uploaded to a claim. A field read with low confidence waits for a claims handler to confirm.
fields.feature_4:
A document checklist on every claim

Every claim carries the list of documents its loss type needs, such as a police report for a theft. Claimants get a reminder with an upload link until the list is complete.
fields.feature_5:
Authority limits written once

A settlement above an adjuster's limit waits for the claims manager, with the estimate beside it. The decision is saved on the claim with the approver's name and the time.
fields.feature_6:
Claim records in a database you own

Claim records live in a database you own, and the code exports to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Change a rule by prompting Emergent, or have an engineer edit it.

fields.tab_content_1:
A burst pipe reported tonight lands with the water adjuster

Ottilie Brandvold opens the loss report at 9:40 p.m., minutes after a pipe bursts under her kitchen sink. She answers one question per screen and adds 6 photos of the floor. The app opens claim CL-20817 and assigns it to Ruairi Osei, who handles water claims, and emails him the photos.
fields.tab_content_2:
Estimate read into fields, VIN sent back for a check

Kettering Collision, the body shop on claim CL-20844, sends its repair estimate as a scanned PDF. The app reads parts of $3,120 and labor of $1,740, for a $4,860 total. The VIN is blurred on the scan and reads at low confidence, so that one field goes to claims handler Marisol Achterberg to check.
fields.tab_content_3:
The last document chased every 3 days until it arrives

Claim CL-20852 is a stolen e-bike, and 2 of its 3 documents are in: the purchase receipt and photos of the cut lock. The police report is still missing. Teodor Lindqvist gets an email with an upload link every 3 days until he sends it, and each reminder is logged on the claim.
fields.tab_content_4:
Settlements over $10,000 wait for the claims manager

Henrike Mbeki settles water claims up to $10,000 on her own. On claim CL-20861 she proposes $14,200 for a flooded basement, so the settlement waits for claims manager Caspian Oyelaran with the estimate attached. He approves it in the app, and the log records his name and the time.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Insurance Claims Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build insurance claims automation that carries a loss report through to an approved settlement.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the loss report form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with one line, such as homeowners water claims or auto physical damage, and write down every step a claim takes from the first report to settlement. Note who touches it at each step and which documents they wait for.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Tell Emergent what a claim record holds, starting with the policy number and the loss date. Name every field an adjuster must confirm by hand, like a VIN read from a phone photo or a total read from a faxed estimate.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for a loss report that works on a phone, one question per screen, with photo upload at the end. Decide which answer sets the loss type, because the loss type is what picks the adjuster and the document checklist.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect your policy or claims system through its API. Each new claim then checks the policy number and dates against the policy record. Emergent builds the sync, and claim status writes back to the system your team already uses.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write each adjuster's settlement authority in plain English, for example $10,000 for staff adjusters and $50,000 for senior adjusters. Add rules for odd cases too, like a claim reported 30 days after the loss going to a senior adjuster.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put twenty claims your team closed last quarter through the app and compare its fields and holds with what happened. Fix each difference by prompting Emergent, then replay the same twenty until every one of them matches.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn the app on for new claims in one line of business while open claims finish the old way. After a month with no corrections, add the next line, starting with the one your adjusters spend the most hours keying today.

faq_plan.a: Insurance claims automation is software that runs the repeat steps of a claim: the first report, then document collection and routing. For a homeowner, that first notice of loss is how the claims process starts. The judgment stays human, because adjusters decide whether an insurance company must pay a claim and, if so, how much.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up insurance claims automation?
faq_plan.a: Map one line of business first, then describe it to Emergent's AI automation builder: the loss report questions, the claim record, who gets which claims, and the settlement limits. Emergent builds the form, the queues, and the database from that prompt, and you change any rule by prompting again. Replay claims you already closed before new ones go through it.

faq_plan.q: Which parts of insurance workflow automation should stay with an adjuster?
faq_plan.a: Keep coverage and payment decisions with your adjusters. One of their duties is to determine whether the insurance policy covers the loss claimed. Automate the work around it instead: intake, assignment, document chasing, and holds above a limit. Emergent builds apps that read documents into fields and send low-confidence fields to a person.

faq_plan.q: Can insurance claims automation also track premiums that policyholders owe?
faq_plan.a: It can, as a separate workflow. Premiums owed to you are receivables, and accounts receivable automation fits them better than a claims queue: due dates and payment reminders. If both live in one app, store premiums apart from claims. That way a payment reminder and a claim update reach the policyholder as different messages.

faq_plan.q: What should the loss report in insurance claims automation ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the policy number, when and where the loss happened, a description of the damage, and photos. One home insurer's glossary lists the date, time, and location of the incident, plus a description of the damage, as information to provide. Put photo upload last. A slow phone connection on site then cannot cost the policyholder the answers above it.

faq_plan.q: Can insurance claims automation read repair estimates and invoices?
faq_plan.a: Yes. With Emergent you build an app that reads documents such as invoices and forms into structured fields, and any field read with low confidence goes to a person to check. On a repair estimate that means the parts, labor, total, and VIN land on the claim without retyping. Start with a strict confidence threshold and loosen it once the checks come back clean.

faq_plan.q: How does insurance claims automation send settlements to accounting?
faq_plan.a: Through the accounting system's API. The app sends each approved settlement to your ledger with the claim number and the payee, and reads back the payment status. Posting entries and closing the month are accounting automation work. That can run in the same app or in one your finance team owns.

faq_plan.q: Is claim data safe in insurance claims automation built with AI?
faq_plan.a: It can be, with access set up well. Emergent has SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001, and the data stays in a database you own. Inside the app, set access by role: adjusters see their own queue, and only the claims manager opens settlement approvals. Have your security lead review those access rules before live claims go through the app.

faq_plan.q: How long should I test insurance claims automation before going live?
faq_plan.a: Test until a replay of closed claims matches what your team did. Twenty claims from last quarter, across every loss type the app handles, make a good first set; include odd ones, like a late report or a claim with two vehicles. Run each odd case twice to confirm the result holds.

faq_plan.q: Will insurance claims automation cut retyping between email and the claims system?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for the data the app collects or reads itself. Loss report answers go straight into the claim record, and documents uploaded to a claim are read into fields. Adjusters no longer copy them out of email threads. For a backlog of paper files that sits outside the claims flow, data entry automation is the closer fit.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Insurance Claims Automation for Your Claims Team', title 'Build Insurance Claims Automation | Emergent', hero 'Get insurance claims automation that opens each claim from the first report and assigns the right adjuster.' (107 chars) cover the whole claims job; how-to description is one sentence carrying the primary.

intent.evidence: Informational, explainer-heavy SERP: FAQ 1 defines the term ('software that runs the repeat steps of a claim'), four tabs show intake, estimate reading, document chasing and settlement approval, seven how-to steps from 'Pick one line of business' to 'Switch on new claims'.

specificity.evidence: Claims-desk vocabulary throughout: 'loss type and territory', 'authority limits', 'police report for a theft', 'homeowners water claims or auto physical damage', 'a claim reported 30 days after the loss going to a senior adjuster'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Policyholders answer one question per screen...', 'Kettering Collision, the body shop on claim CL-20844, sends...', 'Henrike Mbeki settles water claims up to $10,000 on her own.'

craft.evidence: Two ', so' endings (tab_content_2, tab_content_4) are within the QC limit and recorded as a note; no blocking craft class.

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail ('a pipe bursts under her kitchen sink', 'photos of the cut lock', 'a total read from a faxed estimate'); one voice note on FAQ 1 recorded.

truth.evidence: BLS spans match: FAQ 1 'adjusters decide whether an insurance company must pay a claim and, if so, how much' = BLS 'They decide whether an insurance company must pay a claim and if so, how much'; FAQ 3 'determine whether the insurance policy covers the loss claimed' = BLS duty line; Kin FNOL spans match FAQ 1 and FAQ 5. Emergent claims map to approved ids (ai-extraction, alerts, api-connect, soc2-iso 'SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001', database-owned, code-export on paid plans, conversational, free-start, no-caps). No coverage, legal or compliance advice: 'Whether a loss is covered stays a decision people make.' Tab 2 numbers add up: $3,120 + $1,740 = $4,860.

distinct.evidence: Insurance-only stories (CL-20817 burst pipe, CL-20844 body-shop estimate, CL-20852 stolen e-bike, CL-20861 flooded basement); sibling primaries appear only as FAQ link anchors (accounts receivable automation, accounting automation, data entry automation), never as headings.

faq.evidence: 10 questions, all ending '?', no brand or file-format asks; hub link in item 2; three sibling links in items 4, 7, 10; secondary 'insurance workflow automation' in Q3; moat lines in items 3, 6, 8. Q1 PA7 gate reject is a gate issue for Divit, not a page defect.
